memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "All the nations will ask: 'Why has the Lord done this to this land? Why this fierce, burning anger?' And the answer will be: 'It is because this people abandoned the covenant of the Lord, the God of their ancestors, the covenant he made with them when he brought them out of Egypt.'" — Deut 29:24-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses anticipates the question the nations would ask when they saw the ruined land: "Why has the Lord done this?" And he gives the answer plainly: "because this people abandoned the covenant of the Lord." The tragedy was not arbitrary. It flowed from one root cause — they abandoned the God who had rescued them.

Notice how the answer points back to grace received and then spurned. This was the God "who brought them out of Egypt." He had saved them, made them His own, showered them with faithfulness. And they walked away from Him. The heartbreak of the passage is the heartbreak of abandoned love.

This searches our own hearts. God's greatest concern is not merely that we break rules, but that we abandon Him — that we turn from the One who loved and rescued us. Sin, at its root, is a relational betrayal. It is leaving the God who has been nothing but faithful.

But here the gospel offers such hope. Even when His people abandon Him, God does not stop pursuing them. The whole story of Scripture is of a faithful God chasing after an unfaithful people. And in Christ, He went to the furthest lengths to win us back, dying for us "while we were still sinners" (Rom 5:8). If you have wandered from God, know this: the covenant-keeping God still calls you home. His faithfulness is greater than your failure. Return to Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I see sin as a betrayal of the God who loves me, not just rule-breaking?
2. Have I in any way wandered from the God who rescued me?
3. How does God's pursuing love encourage me to return to Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Faithful God, forgive me for the times I have wandered from You who rescued me. Thank You that Your love pursues me still, even to the cross. Draw my wandering heart home. Amen.
